title: 3D Rendering in New York: Product and Interior | 22 Signals
description: 3D rendering for New York developers, brands and designers: photoreal interiors, amenity floors, packaging and product images, delivered before the shoot.
h1: 3D rendering for New York developers, brands and designers who need the image before the thing exists
intro: 22 Signals produces 3D rendering New York developers and brands use when there is nothing to photograph yet: photoreal interiors and amenity spaces for buildings under construction, packaging and product renders for launches, campaign visuals, and 3D models for websites and ads. We work from your drawings, CAD files or samples, remotely from London, on a written schedule.

sections.h: Selling what is not built yet
p: New York sells a lot of things before they exist. Condominium towers in Hudson Yards, Long Island City and downtown Brooklyn go to market from a sales gallery while the frame is still going up. A beauty brand in the Flatiron District needs launch images months before the first production run. A jewelry designer on 47th Street wants to show a ring in five metals without casting five rings. A furniture maker needs a catalog for NYCxDesign in May.

Photography cannot help in any of those cases. That is why so much of the 3D rendering New York firms buy shows things that are still on paper. Good rendering fills the gap, and in many cases it is also quicker to change: a new finish, a new colorway or a new angle is an edit, not a reshoot.

list: Photoreal product renders for e-commerce, Amazon and retailer listings, on white or in context
Packaging renders for launches, retailer pitches and investor decks
Campaign visuals: hero images and scenes that would be costly or impossible to shoot
Interior visualization for residences, model units, lobbies, amenity floors and retail fit-outs
Architectural visualization of exteriors and street views from your architect's model
3D models for web and ads: turntable spins, configurators and assets for animation

sections.h: Real estate rendering for the New York market
p: Residential buyers in the city judge a building on its interiors, its amenities and its views, so that is where the rendering effort goes. We build model units with the actual finish schedule, render lobbies and amenity floors at different times of day, and create view studies from upper floors using photography you supply or commission.

For renovation and townhouse projects, such as a Brooklyn brownstone conversion, renders help owners, boards and buyers agree on a design before work starts. For commercial owners, renders of a repositioned lobby or a built-out floor help leasing teams talk to tenants months earlier.
Sales materials often go to counsel before release, so we keep a dated version log of every image and the drawings it was based on.

sections.h: Product and brand rendering for fashion, beauty and retail
list: Beauty and fragrance: bottles, compacts and tubes with accurate glass, liquid and metallic finishes
Fashion accessories: bags, footwear and eyewear in every colorway from one model
Jewelry and watches: metals, stones and close-up detail at sizes no camera can match easily
Consumer goods and DTC brands: product pages, comparison images and exploded views
Retail: window and store concepts for SoHo, Madison Avenue or pop-up spaces before the build

p: We work with New York companies remotely from London, and rendering is well suited to it. You send drawings, CAD or SketchUp files, finish schedules, samples or reference photos; we send back clay renders for layout approval, then textured drafts, then finals. Reviews happen in a shared tool where you mark up the image directly.

New York is five hours behind London for most of the year, so comments sent at the end of your day are often addressed by your next morning. Physical samples, such as a fabric swatch or a bottle, can be couriered to us. We visit New York when the project needs it, for example to see a site or a showroom. Final files arrive in the sizes and formats each channel needs, from print-ready sales brochures and billboard crops to compressed web images, so nobody on your side has to resize anything.

sections.h: Proof: holding the scope on visual work
p: We have managed over $1.5 million in projects, and on visual work the thing that protects budgets is a clear approval path. Every rendering job runs through fixed stages, layout, materials, lighting and finals, with a sign-off at each. Changes before a stage is approved are part of the job; changes after it are scoped and dated before we make them. That keeps launch dates intact.

sections.h: How we work: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: what the images are for, where they will appear and the date they are needed. Plan: shot list, camera angles, inputs required and a written schedule. Build: modeling, materials, lighting and rendering, with your review at each stage. Grow: reuse the models for animation, configurators, ads and the next season, so each new image costs less effort than the first.

list: Detail and complexity of the model, and whether CAD files exist
Interior or exterior, and how much furniture, styling and context each scene needs
Material accuracy, such as glass, liquids, fabrics or gemstones
Extra outputs: animation, turntable spins or web-ready models

p: Rendering studios stop at the image. We can take the same 3D model into a launch film, an animated explainer, a paid social campaign or an interactive product page, because animation, video, ads and web development sit in the same team. For a New York developer that can mean renders, a building film, a sales website and the ads that drive inquiries, from one brief. Related: video and animation, web development, paid media and 3D animation.

faqs.q: What files do you need to start a rendering project?
faqs.a: For architecture and interiors: plans, elevations, a 3D model if your architect has one, and a finish schedule. For products: CAD files if available, otherwise dimensioned drawings, photos and physical samples. We tell you exactly what is missing after a first look, so nothing stalls once work begins.

faqs.q: Can you render New York condo interiors and amenity floors?
faqs.a: Yes. Model units, lobbies, amenity floors and view studies are a large part of residential rendering, and we build them from your architect's drawings and finish schedules. We keep a dated version log of each image and its source drawings, which helps when sales materials go to counsel for review.

faqs.q: Are renders as convincing as photography for products?
faqs.a: For most products, yes, and often more flexible. Glass, metal, liquids and fabrics can be rendered photoreal, and one model can produce every colorway and angle. Food, people and very soft textures are harder; where a photo would be better, we say so.

faqs.q: Do you need to visit our site or showroom in New York?
faqs.a: Usually not. Drawings, models, samples and reference photos are enough for most jobs. When seeing a space would change the result, such as a complex existing interior, we can visit New York when the project needs it, agreed at the planning stage.

faqs.q: Can the 3D models be used for animation and websites?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is one of the main reasons to render rather than shoot. The same model can become a turntable product spin, a configurator on your site, an animated explainer or a building walkthrough film. We plan for reuse at the start so the model is built to the right level of detail.

faqs.q: How much does 3D rendering cost in New York?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of images, model complexity, materials, revisions and deadlines. We do not publish prices. Send us your drawings or product files after a 15-minute call and we will return a written quote with a schedule.
